checks/check-proposal-contract.sh READS these lists rather than

unamended from SPEC-terrain, the placement cover.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982).
The rule these entries are written under - what a copy is, what the two
markers `[implemented-against: ...]` and `[see: ...]` mean, and why nothing
names a section number or a line range - lives in ONE place:
src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md. It is not restated here; fifteen copies of it had
already drifted into eight variants, which is what kogaki#982 collapsed.
THE NAMES THIS FILE USES, and the spec each one names:

label_floor.carried_here: form only — a necessary condition, never sufficiency
label_floor.sufficiency_routes_to: the review lane's judgment half (kogaki#13, story 1.5): whether the stated effect is the effect that occurs, and whether it is in plain register

records_home.suffix_note: the scanner pattern is composed as "*" + suffix; the SUFFIX is the declared key because a bare suffix is what a producer can concatenate, and a glob is not — which is why both writers hardcoded the name for as long as this field was declared as a glob (kogaki#964, carrying kogaki#961)
records_home.rationale: a default carrier, not an enumerated directory — an enumerated home leaves record N+1 uncovered by default
